narratives.claim: Foreign funding of Indian NGOs is dominated by Christian evangelical money aimed at conversion.
narratives.strongestCase: In FY2015-16 four of the top six recipients (Ayana ₹826 cr, Believers ₹343 cr, WVI ₹319 cr, RDT ₹209 cr) were Christian-founded; the two largest donors in FY2011-12 were Compassion International and the LDS Church; in FY2024-25 Christian bodies received ₹1,345 cr against Hindu bodies' ₹328 cr; the US, UK and Germany supply ~70% of FC.
narratives.strongestCounter: Religious-coded receipts are a small minority of the ₹22,974 cr total (₹1,743 cr by named category; at most ₹5,150 cr on the broadest basis); most FC is coded social/educational/health; a Hindu trust (Param Shakti Peeth ₹418 cr) was #2 in FY2015-16; the largest Christian recipients (WVI, Compassion partners, RDT) deliver child sponsorship, hospitals and schools, and RDT states it dismisses staff for conversion activity; 'funding a Christian charity' ≠ 'funding conversion', and the 2026 Rules now define proselytisation out of permitted purpose precisely because the returns did not distinguish it.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Association-wise FC-4 purpose codes (religious vs social) for the top 50 recipients by year; any adjudicated finding (court, not IB note) that FC was used for inducement to convert.

narratives.claim: The NDA government uses FCRA to strangle civil society that criticises it.
narratives.strongestCase: Oxfam India (Jan 2022), CPR (Jan 2024), CARE, Amnesty and Greenpeace all lost FCRA access; CPR's stated ground equated policy reports with current-affairs programming; retired civil servants wrote to the Home Minister about 'needless harassment'; the 2020 Amendment's sub-granting ban and 20% admin cap hit advocacy organisations hardest.

narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: A year-wise table of s.14 cancellations 'for violation' with stated grounds, compared UPA 2011–14 vs NDA 2014–26, and the share of those targets that were advocacy/rights organisations.

narratives.claim: The 2026 FCRA Amendment Bill lets the Union seize church and NGO property.
narratives.strongestCase: The Bill creates a Designated Authority that takes control of FC-funded assets when a certificate is cancelled, surrendered or ceases, may transfer them to ministries/agencies or sell them with proceeds to the Consolidated Fund; ~37,700 registrations are cancelled or expired, so the pool of assets is very large (₹35,968 cr unutilised balances alone).
narratives.strongestCounter: s.15 FCRA 2010 has vested such assets in a State authority since 2010; the Bill requires the religious character of places of worship to be maintained; it cuts the maximum prison term from 5 years to 1; the government's stated purpose is to end the 'limbo' States said they could not manage.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: The JPC report's text on compensation, appeal and the scope of 'assets'; the first uses of the Authority once enacted.

symmetryCheck: Government-critical (Oxfam India, CPR, CARE) and non-critical/aligned (World Vision India, Compassion partners, Believers/Ayana, RDT) recipients were recorded with the same fields: receipts where found, enforcement event, stated ground, response. Result: the largest enforcement events by money fell on service charities that do not criticise the government (Compassion ~₹325 cr/yr; Ayana ₹826 cr; WVI ₹170–319 cr; RDT ₹209 cr), while the critic cases (Oxfam, CPR) carry stated grounds tied to content — the lens produces an alarming picture on BOTH sides, which is a finding about the regime's breadth rather than about targeting. UPA-era control: the Dec 2013 Parliament answer shows the same ministry, same statute, 41,844 registrants with 40% non-filers and ₹11,548 cr receipts — the non-filing problem that drove 91% of later cancellations predates 2014. Aligned-side receipts (Ekal, Sewa, VIF, India Foundation) could not be found at all, so the symmetry on receipts is incomplete and recorded as a void. Domestic control: Azim Premji Foundation alone disburses ₹1,639 cr/yr (7% of all FC), and Bain/Dasra put foreign private giving (~₹23,000 cr) at ~19% of private philanthropy and ~1% of total social-sector spend — foreign money is a minor stream in Indian welfare finance.
